questions.title: Outline the purpose of stubs during the development of a software program (Question 25, CSSA 2024)

items.text: Outline the purpose of stubs during the development of a software program. Include an example in your response.

criteria.criterion: Provides a clear outline of the use of stubs during software development
Provides an outline of the use of stubs during software development
Shows an understanding of stubs

markingRubricContentItem.text:
A stub is a small subroutine used in place of a yet to be coded subroutine. Stubs do not perform any processing. Stubs can be used to set values of variables affecting their calling. Stubs can include output statements to inform the programmer that the call to the subroutine has been successful. 

Creation of stubs is used when a top-down design method is applied, as higher-level subroutines are created before lower level subroutines and it is necessary to create dummy subroutines, enabling the  testing of those higher-level subroutines that are being coded.

questions.title: Provide an example of when a stub and driver may be used in software testing. (Question 22, ITE 2023)

items.text: Provide an example of when a stub and driver may be used in software testing.

criteria.criterion: Provides an example of when a stub AND driver may be used in software testing.
Provides an example of when a stub OR driver may be used in software testing.
Shows some understanding of stubs OR drivers.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
A stub may be used in software testing when you are using a top-down approach, writing top-level modules before lower-level modules. A stub would enable you to write placeholder code for the lower-level modules, allowing the top-level modules which rely on those lower modules to be tested before the lower-level modules are fully implemented. For example, if a game is being developed and part of the required functionality is to validate player names, the stub could be

BEGIN validatePlayerName(pName: String), returns Boolean

RETURN True

END validatePlayerName

This allows the rest of the program to be developed and tested, and the logic for this function to be added later.

A driver may be used in software testing when you wish to test modules of a program in isolation. This is commonly used for unit testing. A driver is written which functions as a test harness, allowing the module to be called and executed, and the result returned to the driver for comparison with the actual, known good result.

For example, if the validatePlayerName function has been written and needs to be tested, the line

PRINT validatePlayerName(“John”)

is an example of a very simple driver.

questions.title: Describe TWO different types of user documentation that should be included with the new software (Question 21, ITE 2022)

items.text:
A car company has a large number of dealerships throughout Australia. New software is being developed for the dealerships which includes the following features:

  • The ability to generate quotes, based on the model of car, extra features and trade-in
  • Search functionality so that specific models of cars can be found at other dealerships
  • Monthly reporting of sales and inventory
  • The ability to type commands from a list of common tasks e.g. monthly_report(07,”NSW”), generate_quote

Describe TWO different types of user documentation that should be included with the new software.

criteria.criterion: Provides features of TWO types of documentation and relates it to the scenario, showing an excellent understanding of user documentation
Provides features of TWO types of documentation with some reference to the scenario,  showing a good understanding of user documentation.
Identifies TWO types of documentation and shows some understanding of user documentation
Shows some understanding of documentation.

sampleAnswerContentItem.text:
User manual. This should contain minimum hardware and software requirements, an installation guide, detailed information about how to use the program and a troubleshooting guide. In this example the installation guide could provide guidance to system administrators on how they could deploy the software to all of their car dealerships automatically. The section on using the program could contain sections on generating quotes and searching for cars, and should include screenshots and explanations of how to use this functionality.

Reference manual. This is an alphabetical list of commands available in the program, along with a brief explanation and examples of use. For example, one of the entries would be: monthly_report(month,state)

Generates a monthly sales report for the given month (two digits e.g. 07 for July) and state (standard abbreviation, e.g. “NSW”).

Example of use: monthly_report(07,”NSW”)

Answers could also include: help file, tutorial or standalone installation guide.

questions.title: Documenting Software Changes and Updates (Question 28, ITE 2021)

items.text:
ABC software produces a utility program for Windows which assists users with backing up specific folders. Twelve months after the initial release of the software, they release an update which fixes some bugs and adds new functionality.

Outline how the changes should be documented.

criteria.criterion: Outlines ways the changes should be documented, showing an understanding of documentation and software maintenance.
Identifies ways changes can documented.
Shows some understanding of documentation.

markingRubricContentItem.text:
Documentation includes:

  • appropriate source code comments and intrinsic documentation for the sections of code that were added or changed, including dates of changes and why changes were made

  • ensuring user documentation such as user manuals, reference guides, help files, tutorials etc reflect the new functionality. For example a section may need to be added to the user manual for the new functionality and include relevant screenshots

  • a version log should be published so users and developers can see version numbers and changes.

questions.title: A programmer reviewing the code is concerned about line 9, and thinks it should be Swap(I, i+1).  Which of the following is correct? (Q15, ITE 2017)

items.text:
Consider the following algorithm

1 BEGIN MyAlgorithm

2 last = array.Length

3 swapped = True

4 WHILE swapped = True

5 swapped = False

6 i = 1

7 WHILE i < last

8 IF array[i] > array[i + 1] THEN

9 Swap(array[i], array[i + 1])

10 swapped = True

11 END IF

12 i = i + 1

13 END WHILE

14 last = last – 1

15 END WHILE

16 MyAlgorithm = array

17 END MyAlgorithm

A programmer reviewing the code is concerned about line 9, and thinks it should be Swap(I, i+1).

Which of the following is correct?

options.text: The programmer reviewing the code is correct.
Both are incorrect, it should be Swap(array[i+1], array[i]).
You cannot tell which is correct unless you examine the code for Swap.
